objective: Improve geometric-mean throughput across the frozen prop_read, array_read, int_arith, regexp_ascii, prop_update, typed_array_read, float_arith, and regexp_utf16 cases selected from upstream tests/microbench.js plus fresh-process ES-module startup. The split-specific pinned Test262 subset, byte-exact observable and module outputs, and stripped qjs binary size no greater than baseline plus 1% are hard gates. Only the interpreter, numeric conversion, regexp, Unicode, utility, and their public/internal header files enumerated by sourceDetails.mutableEnvelope are mutable; the CLI, clock provider, build, evaluator, tests, and workloads are protected.

measurement.platform: linux/arm64 Docker Desktop on Apple M3 Max; final recalibration required on frozen GCE Linux host
measurement.q: reference-normalized geometric mean operations per trusted external wall-second over four split-specific streamed derivatives of upstream microbench.js plus median-of-3-rounds ES-module startup throughput (fastest 16 of each round's 31 trusted-timed fresh-process launches); for each microbenchmark sample the trusted parent COMPOSES a fresh randomized benchmark program (fresh identifiers, object shapes with shuffled insertion order and decoy properties, permuted read/update schedules and dependency graphs, randomized loop directions, index strides, fold expression shapes, and constants; per-iteration scored operation count and workload class preserved) and streams it on stdin at clock-start together with a fresh nonce, randomized input data, and a per-evaluation jittered iteration count, so no fixed public loop exists to pattern-match and nothing structural is visible in the untimed window; the printed nonce-salted running fold must reproduce byte for byte the pristine in-eval trusted-baseline build run on the identical streamed bytes; each leg is reduced to the fastest (min) of 15 round-robin interleaved samples per binary, bracketed by identical reference samples so shared host contention cancels; gaming-resistance cross-checks on every candidate leg use the out-of-process wait4/getrusage(RUSAGE_CHILDREN) CPU accounting read by the trusted parent (hardware perf counters are unavailable in the eval container: perf_event_open(PERF_TYPE_HARDWARE) returns ENOENT on the pinned VM kernel even for root with CAP_SYS_ADMIN): every sample must satisfy cpu <= wall*1.15+0.02s (single-threaded discipline) and each benchmark's kept-fastest candidate CPU must be >= 0.4x the reference's on identical work, bounding unearned throughput to 2.5x (the wall-clock floor of 10x is retained as an outer bound); module-startup rounds carry the same per-launch discipline (1.5x+5ms) and a median kept-CPU floor of 0.4x reference; q = raw_q * 7385110.981771862 / reference_q so ambient host-speed drift cancels

terminalSeal.attestation: Only trusted correctness, deterministic workload construction, feasibility, A-A/noise, sensitivity diagnostics, and exploit-resistance work was performed. No optimizer, mutation search, headroom pilot, or seed-optimizer session received this task identity, repository, fixtures, source tree, scores, or feedback.

exploitReview.protectedPathEscape: broker diff-protects CLI, clock provider, build, evaluator, worker, test, fixture, and metadata paths; evaluator rejects symlinks, non-regular entries, and files absent from the frozen inventory
exploitReview.benchmarkSpecialCasing: train and validation use distinct holdout benchmark selections, Test262 cases, observable programs, and module graphs; the shortcut diagnostic carries the valid inline OP_mod remainder fast path (helping both splits) while a validation-only UTF-16 regexp delay drags its held-out score below baseline, inverting its train ordering
exploitReview.fixtureFingerprinting: terminal assets remain holdout-only and content-hashed; candidate processes run unprivileged after the built source and copied fixtures become root-owned read-only files
exploitReview.outputFabrication: the timed microbenchmark path accepts no sealed closed-form output and no fixed public loop: the trusted parent COMPOSES each sample's whole benchmark program (identifiers, object shapes, decoy properties, read/update schedules, dependency graphs, loop directions, index strides, fold expression shapes, constants) and streams it on stdin at clock-start together with a fresh nonce and randomized input data (never argv/env, so no constructor/.init_array can read anything structural before the interpreter runs, and candidate-writable state is swept between launches so no launch can record a program for a later one); the printed nonce-salted running fold must reproduce byte for byte a pristine in-eval trusted-baseline build run on the identical streamed bytes, so producing it requires evaluating an arbitrary member of the trusted program family rather than replaying a precompiled recurrence. Residual throttled-native-evaluation classes are bounded by the out-of-process work-proportional cross-check: the trusted parent reads each leg's CPU time from the kernel's reaped-child wait4/getrusage accounting (hardware perf counters probed unavailable in the eval container: PERF_TYPE_HARDWARE -> ENOENT on the pinned VM kernel; the CPU-time channel is the strongest available work-proportional signal there), rejects any candidate sample whose CPU exceeds the single-threaded envelope (cpu <= wall*1.15+0.02s, closing thread-parallel wall compression and forked-helper inflation), and rejects any benchmark whose kept-fastest candidate CPU is below 0.4x the pristine reference's on identical work -- a single-threaded process accrues at most one CPU-second per wall-second, so idle- or spin-throttling into the wall band is bounded to 2.5x unearned throughput (the 10x wall floor is kept as an outer bound); module startup carries the same per-launch discipline and a 0.4x median kept-CPU floor against fixed-output fast-exit fabrication. The trusted evaluator also byte-compares independent observable and module outputs on both splits and the pinned Test262 runner exercises the candidate interpreter directly
exploitReview.timerTampering: every streamed microbenchmark job and module-startup round is timed by trusted Python time.monotonic_ns in the parent process from stdin-stream at clock-start to child exit, and every leg's CPU time comes from the parent's own getrusage(RUSAGE_CHILDREN) delta around the single reaped launch; no candidate-provided clock, counter, or in-process report contributes to q or to the plausibility gates, and the microbenchmark result is validated against the pristine reference rather than any candidate-emitted bookkeeping
exploitReview.buildScriptMutation: Makefile, qjs/qjsc/run-test262 CLI sources, generated repl.c, worker, evaluator, toolchain lock, and source inventory are protected; QJSC is pinned to /usr/bin/false so candidate code never executes during build, and every evaluation builds from source on tmpfs
exploitReview.deadCodeBenchmarkBypass: the measured qjs executes the same interpreter core used for byte-exact programs, ES modules, and the frozen Test262 subset before any score is emitted
